# HydroModPy

> HydroModPy computes where groundwater comes out of the ground and which streams it keeps alive, month by month, for a whole catchment. These are its documentation pages. Each line links to a page; llms-full.txt holds the text of all of them.

## Home

- [HydroModPy](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/index.html): A Python toolbox for automated, reproducible, catchment-scale modeling of shallow groundwater.

## User guide

- [A first run](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/index.html): Install HydroModPy, run a first model in under a minute, then run example 04 from its file and from Python.
- [User guide](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/user-guide/index.html): How to use HydroModPy, in three parts. Start with the first one if you are new.
- [Calibrate K on a network](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/calibrate-k.html): Move K until the stream network the water table sustains matches the mapped one.
- [On a cluster](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/cluster.html): A project of many catchments runs on a Slurm cluster from its plan.
- [Concepts](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/concepts.html): Six words name the things on disk. This page is the whole mental model you need before example 04.
- [Example 04](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/example-04.html): Example 04 models the Nançon catchment (Ille-et-Vilaine) with MODFLOW 6, from 2000 to 2002 in monthly stress periods.
- [Coming from version 1](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/from-v1.html): Version 1 was a set of Python scripts. You built a `Watershed` object, called `add_*` and `update_*` methods on it, and ran MODFLOW with `preprocessing_modflow` and `processing_modflow`.
- [Install](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/install.html): HydroModPy needs Python 3.11, 3.12 or 3.13.
- [Many catchments](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/many-catchments.html): A model tuned on one catchment runs on a hundred with the same project.
- [Share a simulation with its data](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/share-a-simulation.html): A run, or a whole project, leaves your workspace as one archive that holds every file it read.
- [Deliver exports](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/how-to/deliver-exports.html): An `[[export]]` block that names `deliver_to` sends the files of that block once the run is sealed, and each copy is recorded in the run.
- [Long transient runs in windows](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/how-to/long-transient-runs-in-windows.html): A transient run over many years in daily periods can take hours.
- [Plan experiments and score them later](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/how-to/plan-and-score-experiments.html): A plan of experiments runs one model at many points of a box of parameters.
- [Replay a run](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/how-to/replay-a-run.html): A replay plays a sealed run again and says whether it gives the same numbers.
- [Run in Docker](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/how-to/run-in-docker.html): The `Dockerfile` of the repository builds a slim image whose entry point is `hmp`, so a container runs the same program as the command line.
- [Run step by step](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/how-to/run-step-by-step.html): A run can stop after any step and continue later.
- [Use your own files](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/how-to/use-your-own-files.html): HydroModPy reads elevation models, hydrography, geology, structures, forcings and observation series from public APIs or from files on disk.
- [Work in the lab](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/how-to/work-in-the-lab.html): A lab opens a `Project` and plays the same steps a run plays, from `validate` to `run_solver`.
- [Write calibration phases](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/how-to/write-calibration-phases.html): This page shows how to split a calibration into phases and how to use a published protocol that writes them for you.
- [Can I check what was run?](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/can-i-check-what-was-run.html): Yes. A result of HydroModPy is not only a map.
- [Conventions of a run](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/conventions.html): A run stores numbers. This page says how to read them: which date reads which period, which sign a flux has, what a station or a zone is called, and how layers and reaches are counted.
- [How sure is the model?](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/how-sure.html): Not completely, and no groundwater model is.
- [Scoring a simulated stream network](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/network-metrics.html): A model makes a network of streams. A map draws another one.
- [Reading the results](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/reading-results.html): This page is a reading guide to the main outputs of example 04 (the Nançon catchment, see What HydroModPy does).
- [How the model makes streams](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/stream-network.html): HydroModPy does not draw rivers. It computes a water table.
- [What HydroModPy does](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/what-it-computes.html): One map and five sentences first. The rest of the page says what the model computes, from what, with which assumptions, and when not to use it.
- [What “validated” means here](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/what-validated-means.html): The word validated is used loosely. In this documentation it has a narrow meaning.
- [Where the data come from](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/where-the-data-come-from.html): A result is only as good as its inputs. This page names the data that HydroModPy can read, who produces them, how fine they are, and what to do about their licences.

## Reference

- [Command line](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/index.html): $ hmp [-h] [-V] [-w WORKSPACE] <command> ...
- [Reference](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/index.html)
- [`[calibration]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/index.html): Top-level `[calibration]` section.
- [`[data]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/index.html): Top-level `[data]` configuration for the data variables.
- [`[flow]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/index.html): Flow-process configuration.
- [`[flow.sinks_sources]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/sinks_sources/index.html): Top-level container for all sink/source elements of the flow process.
- [TOML parameters](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/index.html): Every section of the configuration file, generated from the models.
- [Python API](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/index.html): import hydromodpy as hmp
- [Calibration methods and metrics](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/calibration-methods.html): Every search method a calibration file can name, and every metric an objective block can score with.
- [Register of changes](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/changes-register.html): The register is the file `hydromodpy/schema/changes.toml`.
- [What changed in the TOML](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/changes.html): Fields added, renamed, removed or changed between two versions.
- [`hmp calibrate`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/calibrate.html): Uses hmp.calibrate().
- [`hmp campaign`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/campaign.html): $ hmp campaign [-h] <action> ...
- [`hmp catalog`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/catalog.html): Uses hmp.trash().
- [`hmp check`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/check.html): Uses hmp.check().
- [`hmp completion`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/completion.html): $ hmp completion [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] {bash,zsh,fish}
- [`hmp config`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/config.html): $ hmp config [-h] {template,figures,resolve,schema,targets,wizard,validate-field,check} ...
- [`hmp data`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/data.html): $ hmp data [-h] <action> ...
- [`hmp diff`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/diff.html): Uses hmp.compare().
- [`hmp doctor`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/doctor.html): Uses hmp.doctor().
- [`hmp example`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/example.html): Uses hmp.example().
- [Exit codes](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/exit-codes.html): A command ends with the code of its outcome.
- [`hmp export`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/export.html): Uses hmp.export(), hmp.open().
- [`hmp install-binaries`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/install-binaries.html): $ hmp install-binaries [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--subset SUBSET] [--mf6-prt] [--to DIR] [--release RELEASE]...
- [`hmp ls`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/ls.html): Uses hmp.status().
- [What a program reads](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/machine-output.html): This page is the interface of `hmp` for a script or a platform.
- [`hmp privacy`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/privacy.html): $ hmp privacy [-h] <action> ...
- [`hmp project`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/project.html): $ hmp project [-h] <action> ...
- [`hmp publish`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/publish.html): Uses hmp.publish().
- [`hmp replay`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/replay.html): Uses hmp.replay().
- [`hmp run`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/run.html): Uses hmp.check(), hmp.run().
- [`hmp show`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/show.html): Uses hmp.show(), hmp.open().
- [`hmp site`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/site.html): $ hmp site [-h] <action> ...
- [`hmp spinup`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/spinup.html): Uses hmp.spinup().
- [`hmp stop`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/stop.html): Uses hmp.stop().
- [`hmp workspace`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/workspace.html): $ hmp workspace [-h] <action> ...
- [Data sources](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/data-sources.html): Every data section of the file, and the sources its `source` key accepts, with who publishes each one and under which licence.
- [Figure requests](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/figure-requests.html): Every table on this page is read from the code of the figure path when the site is built.
- [Glossary](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/glossary.html): The terms used in this part of the site, with a short definition.
- [Outputs of a run](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/outputs.html): A run stores its field arrays in `fields.zarr` and its station series in `tables.parquet/timeseries.parquet`.
- [Calibrable parameters](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibrable.html): A calibration moves the keys below. Name one in `calibration.parameters.<name>.path` and give its range in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`, in the unit the key declares.
- [`[calibration.aggregate]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/aggregate.html): How several scored targets become one cost.
- [`[[calibration.objective_blocks]]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/objective_blocks.html): Weighted metric block used by a composite objective.
- [`[calibration.outputs]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/outputs.html): Named observables extracted from each candidate run.
- [`[calibration.parameters]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/parameters.html): User declaration for one calibrated parameter.
- [`[[calibration.phases]]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/phases.html): One stage of a calibration that runs in several.
- [`[calibration.protocol]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/protocol.html): What a file may say about the protocol beyond naming it.
- [`[calibration.uncertainty]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/uncertainty.html): How wide the search says its own answer is.
- [`[calibration.validation_window]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/validation_window.html): Dates bounding the samples a metric is computed on.
- [`[calibration.window]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/window.html): Dates bounding the samples a metric is computed on.
- [`[data.crossings]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/crossings.html): Top-level crossings variable configuration.
- [`[data.curve_number]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/curve_number.html): SCS curve number raster, read by the soil reservoir.
- [`[data.dem]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/dem.html): Top-level DEM variable configuration.
- [`[data.etp]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/etp.html): Top-level potential evapotranspiration configuration.
- [`[data.geology]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/geology.html): Top-level geology variable configuration.
- [`[data.humidity]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/humidity.html): Top-level relative-humidity configuration.
- [`[data.hydrography]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/hydrography.html): Top-level hydrography configuration.
- [`[data.hydrometry]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/hydrometry.html): Top-level hydrometry configuration.
- [`[data.impervious]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/impervious.html): Sealed share of the ground, read by the soil reservoir as its impervious fraction.
- [`[data.infiltration_ratio]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/infiltration_ratio.html): Infiltration ratio of the soil excess, read by the soil reservoir cell by cell.
- [`[data.intermittency]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/intermittency.html): Top-level intermittency configuration.
- [`[data.lake_abacus]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/lake_abacus.html): Top-level lake-abacus variable configuration.
- [`[data.lake_bathymetry]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/lake_bathymetry.html): Top-level lake-bathymetry variable configuration.
- [`[data.lake_geometry]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/lake_geometry.html): Top-level lake-geometry variable configuration.
- [`[data.lake_inflow]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/lake_inflow.html): Top-level lake-inflow configuration.
- [`[data.lake_levels]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/lake_levels.html): Top-level lake-levels configuration.
- [`[data.lake_outflow]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/lake_outflow.html): Top-level lake-outflow configuration.
- [`[data.lake_withdrawal]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/lake_withdrawal.html): Top-level lake-withdrawal configuration.
- [`[data.layer_base]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/layer_base.html): Top-level layer base variable configuration: one named raster per base.
- [`[data.oceanic]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/oceanic.html): Top-level oceanic configuration.
- [`[data.piezometry]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/piezometry.html): Top-level piezometry configuration.
- [`[data.precipitation]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/precipitation.html): Top-level precipitation configuration.
- [`[data.property_map]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/property_map.html): Top-level property map configuration: one named raster per map.
- [`[data.radiation]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/radiation.html): Top-level radiation configuration.
- [`[data.recharge]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/recharge.html): Top-level recharge configuration.
- [`[data.runoff]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/runoff.html): Top-level runoff configuration.
- [`[data.soil_capacity]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/soil_capacity.html): Soil available water capacity raster, read by the soil reservoir.
- [`[data.soil_moisture]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/soil_moisture.html): Top-level soil-moisture configuration.
- [`[data.substratum]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/substratum.html): Top-level substratum variable configuration.
- [`[data.temperature]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/temperature.html): Top-level air-temperature configuration.
- [`[data.water_quality]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/water_quality.html): Top-level water quality configuration.
- [`[data.wind]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/wind.html): Top-level wind-speed configuration.
- [`[display]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/display.html): Display behavior resolved from the `[display]` TOML section.
- [`[domain]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/domain.html): Domain configuration: the zones, the depth of the aquifer and its layering.
- [`[edition]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/edition.html): The set of defaults the file is read with.
- [`[[export]]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/export.html): One export: what to write, when, in which format, where.
- [`[flow.bc]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/bc.html): Mapping of flow boundary-condition payloads parsed from `[flow.bc]`.
- [`[flow.ic]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/ic.html): Container for flow initial conditions stored in process runtime.
- [`[flow.param]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/param.html): Flow parameter payload using native field-param sections.
- [`[flow.restart_from]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/restart_from.html): The run a hotstart reads, by id and by path: the table form of `restart_from`.
- [`[flow.sinks_sources.etp]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/sinks_sources/etp.html): Typed payload for diffuse evapotranspiration over the model domain.
- [`[flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/sinks_sources/flow_barriers.html): Typed payload for one MODFLOW 6 horizontal flow barrier (HFB).
- [`[flow.sinks_sources.lakes]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/sinks_sources/lakes.html): Typed boundary-condition payload for one MODFLOW 6 LAK lake.
- [`[flow.sinks_sources.recharge]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/sinks_sources/recharge.html): Typed payload for diffuse recharge over the model domain.
- [`[flow.sinks_sources.sfr]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/sinks_sources/sfr.html): Typed boundary-condition payload for one MODFLOW 6 SFR stream network.
- [`[flow.sinks_sources.wells]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/sinks_sources/wells.html): Typed payload for one pumping or injection well.
- [`[geographic]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/geographic.html): Geographic configuration for watershed delineation.
- [The grammar of a HydroModPy file](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/grammar.html): One TOML file describes a run. Its sections are listed in TOML parameters; this page gives the rules they all share: tables, inheritance, quantities, dates, paths, free keys and profiles.
- [`[mesh]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/mesh.html): The mesh engine and the sizes it meshes the model with.
- [`[metrics]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/metrics.html): The station and the window the scores of a run are computed on.
- [Minimal files](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/minimal-files.html): For each section, the smallest file that holds it: the sections every file needs, then the keys the section requires, each with its example value or its default.
- [`[observation]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/observation.html): Configuration for `[observation]`: points sampled during the run.
- [`[overview]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/overview.html): Overview report settings (watershed identity card).
- [`[publication]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/publication.html): The licence and the authorship written into every publication.
- [Find a key by what it measures](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/quantities.html): Every user key whose unit or form the code declares, grouped by kind of quantity.
- [`[recharge_estimates]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/recharge_estimates.html): Recharge estimated from the loaded data, to compare with the run's own.
- [`[simulation]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/simulation.html): Minimal orchestration block declared under `[simulation]`.
- [`[site]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/site.html): The catchment a project models, declared once for every key that needs it.
- [`[sites]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/sites.html): The catchments of a project and the recipes run on each of them.
- [`[solver]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/solver.html): The flow solver of a run, its settings, and the switches every backend may read.
- [`[spinup]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/spinup.html): Settings for the cyclic spin-up loop (`[spinup]`).
- [`[transport]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/transport.html): The `[transport]` section: one table per transport solver the document names.
- [`[workflow]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/workflow.html): Workflow selector configuration.
- [`[workspace]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/workspace.html): Strict-binary workspace configuration.
- [`CalibrationPlan`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/CalibrationPlan.html)
- [`CalibrationReport`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/CalibrationReport.html): session_id,
- [`Catalog`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/Catalog.html): Examples
- [`Comparison`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/Comparison.html)
- [`Diagnostic`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/Diagnostic.html): path,
- [`DoctorReport`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/DoctorReport.html)
- [`ExampleEntry`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/ExampleEntry.html): id,

- [`StatusReport`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/StatusReport.html)
- [`Workspace`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/Workspace.html)
- [Exceptions and error codes](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/exceptions.html): The classes of `hydromodpy.core.exceptions` all derive from `HydroModPyError`.

- [`hmp.publish()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-publish.html): Found in the code
- [`hmp.replay()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-replay.html): Found in the code
- [`hmp.run()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-run.html): Found in the code
- [`hmp.show()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-show.html): Found in the code
- [`hmp.spinup()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-spinup.html): Found in the code
- [`hmp.status()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-status.html): Found in the code
- [`hmp.stop()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-stop.html): Found in the code
- [`hmp.trash()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-trash.html): Found in the code
- [Objects and how they relate](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/objects.html): A run is a folder on disk: field arrays in Zarr, tables in Parquet, under `<project>/runs/<name>/`.
- [Solvers](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/solvers.html): Every process a run can plan and the solver that carries it out, read from the solver registry of the code.

## Theory

- [Theory](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/index.html): Theory covers what HydroModPy computes or decides: the rules it applies when it builds a model, the conversions from TOML to solver input, the methods it implements itself, and what it refuses.
- [Bibliography](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/bibliography.html): References cited in the HydroModPy documentation.
- [Boussinesq theory](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/boussinesq.html): This page gives the equations of the in-house Boussinesq solver, in the order the code applies them, with what they assume and where they stop being true.
- [The inverse problem of a calibration](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/calibration/inverse-problem-formulation.html): A calibration turns a question about the site, such as “which conductivity makes the model reproduce the gauge and the mapped streams?”, into the search for the minimum, or the root, of one number...
- [Downslope distance between two networks](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/downslope-distance.html): A mapped stream network and a simulated one rarely coincide.
- [How water leaves the aquifer](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/exits.html): Water enters the saturated zone as recharge and leaves it through a few exits.
- [Drains and evapotranspiration at the top of the model](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/exits/drains-and-et.html): Two exits act at the top of the model. A drain discharges where the water table reaches the ground.
- [Fixed heads: the sea, the rivers and the sides](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/exits/head-boundaries.html): A fixed head takes the head of a cell out of the solution.
- [Lakes and reservoirs](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/exits/lakes.html): A lake is a boundary package laid on the aquifer grid.
- [Routing on the mesh: the descent D](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/exits/routing-on-the-mesh.html): Where the water of a drain goes next is a question of routing.
- [Where the water table reaches the surface](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/exits/simulated-network.html): The model produces sources, not a stream network.
- [Streams and the water mover](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/exits/streams-and-mover.html): A stream network (SFR) routes the water it receives from reach to reach and exchanges water with the aquifer through its bed.
- [Rain and evaporation: the forcing](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/forcing.html): The aquifer model does not see days: it sees stress periods, and one rate per cell for each period.
- [The groundwater flow problem](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/groundwater-flow.html): What head does the aquifer hold, in every cell and at every time?
- [The mesh](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/mesh.html): The solver does not see the DEM. It sees cells, each with one top, one bottom and one center.
- [Notation](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/notation.html): Every symbol of the theory pages, with its unit and the key that sets it.
- [Recharge estimated from the data](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/recharge-estimates.html): A `[recharge_estimates]` section asks for a range of recharge on the catchment, computed from the loaded weather, gauge and piezometers before the solver runs.
- [Science map](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/science-map.html): Each row is one theory page: the modules that compute it, the unit tests of those modules, and the validation cases that check it against a solution.
- [The daily soil reservoir](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/soil-reservoir.html): The soil reservoir turns the daily rain and ETP of a grid into the recharge of a MODFLOW 6 run.
- [The solvers of the aquifer](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/solvers.html): HydroModPy integrates the groundwater flow equation with one of three solvers: MODFLOW 6, MODFLOW-NWT or the in-house Boussinesq solver.
- [From a zone map to the cells](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/solvers/field-to-cell-parameter-transfer.html): A property such as \(K\) is given per zone of a map: geology classes, bands, rings, or the zones of a raster.
- [XT3D on irregular meshes](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/solvers/xt3d-on-irregular-disv-meshes.html): The two-point flux of (25) is exact when the line between two cell centers is perpendicular to the shared face and the conductivity is the same in every horizontal direction.
- [Time alignment of outputs and observations](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/time-alignment.html): A run writes one value per stress period.
- [Validation](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/validation.html): Each check below is a test of `tests/validation/`.

## About

- [About](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/about/index.html): Who builds HydroModPy, how to cite it, where it is used and which version to install.
- [Applications and papers](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/about/applications.html): Studies that used HydroModPy, newest first.
- [Changelog](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/about/changelog.html): Every release of HydroModPy and every change since the last one, newest first.
- [Cite](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/about/cite.html): If HydroModPy supports your work, cite the technical note.
- [Versions and stability](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/about/versions.html): This site documents version 2.0.1. Published versions are listed on PyPI.
- [Work with us](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/about/work-with-us.html): HydroModPy is open research software under the EPL-2.0 licence.

## Optional

- [Recipes](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/index.html): Each recipe answers “I want to add X: where does it go and what contract must I honor?”.
- [Architecture](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/index.html): How the code is organized: the layers and their allowed imports, the packages, the storage layout and the subsystems.
- [Packages](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/index.html): One page per top-level subpackage of `hydromodpy/`.
- [Documentation](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/documentation/index.html): This site is built from the code as much as the code allows.
- [Contribute](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/index.html): This part is for people who change HydroModPy itself.
- [Project](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/project/index.html): How the project is checked, tested and released, and where it is going.
- [Contracts and design patterns](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/contracts.html): This page says which names the contract of Versions and stability covers: the public import paths, the plugin ports, the two storage Protocols and the field registry.
- [Data scopes and schema evolution](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/data-scopes.html): HydroModPy keeps its state in two scopes: the data folder of a workspace and the project.
- [MODFLOW and Boussinesq backends](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/engines/backends.html): This note says what the three flow backends share, what a MODFLOW build must honor, and the pitfalls of the shared code.
- [Boussinesq engines and experimental closures](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/engines/boussinesq-engines.html): The equations of the Boussinesq solver are on Boussinesq theory, and the solvers side by side are on The solvers of the aquifer.
- [Calibration internals](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/engines/calibration-internals.html): This note is for a contributor who changes `hydromodpy/calibration/`.
- [Mesh engines](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/engines/mesh-engines.html): A mesh engine turns one request into one cell mesh.
- [The mesh pivot and the cell mesh](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/engines/mesh-pivot.html): @dataclass(frozen=True)
- [Processes and boundaries](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/engines/processes-and-boundaries.html): This note says how a validated configuration becomes the objects a solver reads, and how the flow boundary conditions travel along that path.
- [Supports and the simulated network](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/engines/stream-network-support.html): This note covers two things a heterogeneous model needs.
- [From TOML to solver outputs](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/engines/toml-to-solver.html): This note follows the main execution chain, from one TOML file to the solver outputs and the stored run.
- [CI workflows](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/ci.html): Built from `.github/workflows/*.yml` each time the site is built.
- [Environment variables](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/environment.html): Built from `hydromodpy/core/runtime/env.py`; the files that read each variable come from a scan of the code each time the site is built.
- [Optional dependencies](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/extras.html): Built from `[project.optional-dependencies]` of `pyproject.toml` each time the site is built.
- [Architecture gates](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/guards.html): Built from the module docstrings of `tests/unit/architecture/test_*.py` and the YAML contracts beside them each time the site is built.
- [Layer graph](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/layers.html): Built from `tests/unit/architecture/layer_matrix.yaml` each time the site is built.
- [Packages and registries](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/packages.html): Built from the registries of the code and the folders of `hydromodpy/` each time the site is built.
- [Storage tree](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/storage-tree.html): Built from `hydromodpy/results/storage/contract.py`, `hydromodpy/core/state/layout.py` and `hydromodpy/schema/generated_views.py` each time the site is built.
- [Test inventory](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/tests.html): Built from the test files of `tests/`, read without running them, and `pytest.ini` each time the site is built.
- [Add a block to the HTML report](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-block-html-report.html): Use this recipe to add a block to a report page, or to change which figures a preset shows.
- [Add a calibration method](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-calibration-method.html): Calibration runs an ask/tell loop. An optimizer proposes a parameter point, the engine evaluates it, and the optimizer ingests the result.
- [Add a CLI command](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-cli-command.html): The `hmp` and `hydromodpy` commands share the dispatcher in `hydromodpy/cli/main.py`.
- [Add a config field](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-config-field.html): Every TOML knob in HydroModPy is backed by a Pydantic v2 model that forbids extra keys.
- [Add a data source](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-data-source.html): A source is one value a user may write in `source =` for an existing variable.
- [Add a data variable](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-data-variable.html): A data variable is one `[data.<name>]` section of a project TOML, loaded by one variable class and stored in the input cache.
- [Add a figure](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-figure.html): A figure is a request. It names a variable, a preset or a list of panels, in TOML (`[[display.figure]]`), in Python (`run.figure(...)`) or on the command line (`hmp show RUN --figure NAME`).
- [Add a process](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-process.html): A process is a kind of run of the plan of a simulation, with the solvers and the options that serve it.
- [Add a solver](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-solver.html): A solver is one class bound to the key `<process_type>_<name>`, for example `flow_modflow6` or `transport_mt3dms`.
- [Add a test](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-test.html): The test tree under `tests/` has one folder per family.
- [Add an exporter](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-an-exporter.html): Exporters convert simulation results into external file formats.
- [Build a frontend](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/build-a-frontend.html): HydroModPy is a Python library. Its wheel ships no HTTP server, no FastAPI binding and no websocket.
- [Cut a release](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/cut-a-release.html): A release is a Git tag. The tag starts three jobs: the publication to PyPI, the GitHub Release, and the build of the documentation for that version.
- [Fix a failing architecture gate](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/fix-an-architecture-gate.html): python -m pytest tests/unit/architecture -q -n 2
- [Plug into a port](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/plug-into-a-port.html): A port is a place where HydroModPy takes a class it does not know in advance: a solver backend, an output extractor, a data source, a trial evaluator, an optimizer, a terrain engine, a mesh engine,...
- [Serve over HTTP](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/serve-over-http.html): The repository keeps a thin HTTP layer beside the wheel, `hydromodpy_server/`.
- [Layered architecture](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/layered-architecture.html): HydroModPy is a layered dependency graph.
- [Mental model and design choices](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/mental-model.html): This page explains why HydroModPy is split into several layers instead of collapsing everything into one execution object.
- [Package: calibration](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/calibration.html): Fitting model parameters to observations.
- [Package: catchment](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/catchment.html): The catchment layer takes a DEM and an outlet and gives the catchment, its river network and the ground the model sits on.
- [Package: cli](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/cli.html): The command line, with the `hmp` and `hydromodpy` entry points.
- [Package: config](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/config.html): The root of the configuration.
- [Package: core](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/core.html): The kernel leaf of HydroModPy. Every other package may read `core`, and `core` reads no sibling package, not even under `TYPE_CHECKING`.
- [Package: data](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/data.html): Everything a run reads from outside is here: provider APIs, the files of the user, their cache and the typed records handed to the layers above.
- [Package: display](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/display.html): A figure is a `FigureRequest` from `request.py`.
- [Package: mesh](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/mesh.html): This package turns a project into the cells that MODFLOW 6 and the other solvers compute on.
- [Package: model](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/model.html): The model is what a groundwater solver reads, written without any solver.
- [Package: project](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/project.html): The public face of HydroModPy.
- [Package: results](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/results.html): What a run leaves on disk and how it is read back.
- [Package: schema](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/schema.html): The shapes that HydroModPy writes for a reader outside this process.
- [Package: solver](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/solver.html): The numerical backends. `solver.backend` names the flow backend, the table `[solver.<name>]` holds its settings, and a `[[simulation.process]]` entry names the solvers each process runs.
- [Package: validity_frame](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/validity_frame.html): It is outside the stable public API and has no compatibility guarantee.
- [Package: workflow](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/workflow.html): The order in which a project is built and run.
- [Pipeline resume from artifacts](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/pipeline_resume.html): The simulation pipeline rebuilds its in-memory state exclusively from durable artifacts and the TOML config.
- [Storage layout](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/storage-layout.html): Disk is the truth. The database is an index rebuilt from disk.
- [Docstring policy](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/docstring-policy.html): The Python API reference is generated from the code.
- [Documentation coverage](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/documentation/coverage.html): What the models leave undocumented, computed at each build from the field registry.
- [How the docs are built](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/documentation/how-the-docs-are-built.html): The site is a Sphinx 9 project in `docs/source/`, with the PyData theme 0.23 and MyST 5.1.
- [Contributor handbook](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/handbook.html): How to report a problem, set up a development environment, follow the coding style, run the tests and send a change.
- [Reading a failing check](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/project/ci-workflows.html): HydroModPy has one pull-request gate and a set of focused workflows under `.github/workflows/`.
- [Tests](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/project/tests.html): HydroModPy splits tests into families because they answer different questions.
- [Quick start](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/quick-start.html): Ten minutes from a clone to a first commit.
- [Roadmap](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/roadmap.html): The issue tracker is the live source of truth for work in flight.
- [Write a theory page](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/write-a-theory-page.html): A theory page gives the equations of one model, in the order the code applies them, with their assumptions and their limits.
